input: Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter, Space, arrows and typing; no pointer actions or programmatic focus
limitations: Internal authored campaign, not blind or fresh-player observation. Synthetic viewport and pagehide, not physical hardware or app switch. Voice completion and cleanup do not establish listening quality. Transition times include UI review/reloads; they are not INP or field percentiles.

observations.text:
Rain runs down the inside of Kite City’s dome. Above it, Helion’s towers stay dry. Below it, your chip lights up: “Ward Four noodle stall. Tonight. I have work.” Quill, a broker. You need the work. You have not said yes.

The year is 3055. You carry things, open doors, find what someone would rather lose. People call you a runner. Across the street, a Glass Chapel advertisement promises a night without regret: pay to edit an hour of memory. The original survives in a sliver of glass called a shard.

The stall’s amber light cuts through the rain a few streets ahead. Find Quill. Hear the offer before you decide what it is worth.

choices.text:
1

2
Go straight to Quill’s meeting.
Details
Skip the prologue and hear the job. No money, items, or stats change.

observations.text:
You used to cross the city above the rain, a Helion badge opening every door ahead of you. Then your clearance stopped working. Down here, you are learning what those doors kept outside. Your old training is still yours.

Your chip holds 60 creds. Quill covered a shortfall once. The debt still carries his name, and his invitation arrived before you found another way to pay it.

You still reach for the old badge at locked doors. You would like a life that does not need it. Quill brokers jobs without an official record. Tonight you are going to hear one, under the street handle Threshold. What do you want it to buy?

observations.text:
You want work without another claim on your name. Steam rises through the awnings. A woman behind the noodle counter wipes rain off a menu while the tower advert plays above her: “Sleep without yesterday.” She sees you looking.

“Funny thing to sell,” she says. “Yesterday.”

Quill sits at the far end of her counter, coat buttoned, bowl untouched. He raises two fingers. You have a moment before you take the stool.

choices.text:
1
Ask her what she means.
Details
Hear one person’s experience of the memory trade. No check or purchase.

2
Take the stool opposite Quill.

observations.text:
“A regular came in last winter,” she says. “He'd sold an argument with his wife to make the rent. Remembered getting paid. Didn't remember what he needed to apologize for. Asked me to write it down.”

She flattens the damp menu. “I sell dinner. But if someone hires you to carry an hour, ask whose it was before you ask what it pays.”

Quill moves his bowl aside. You still need work; now you have a question to take with you.

choices.text:
1
Sit down and hear Quill’s offer.

observations.text:
Quill moves his bowl aside. "Threshold. Mara Voss, Helion logistics. Glass Chapel edits her memory at dawn. Bring me the original hour, intact. Fifty now, two hundred on delivery. Her bodyguard is Kerr. He is paid to stop you."

You came because the city already has too much say over who you are. The work is a means, not a claim on your name. He knows the tab. He does not mention it, which is how Quill mentions things.

The stallholder’s story stays with you. Whose hour are you being asked to carry? Quill has not touched his dinner. You have not agreed to the job.

Quill turns the untouched bowl away from the edge. "Do not give me an easy yes. I need you to come back with the hour."

observations.text:
Fifty is on your chip. The rest of the city will try to take it. You tell Quill your name stays yours. "The front desk will ask for one," he says. "The other doors ask different questions."

"Three ways in. The front sells forgiveness to anyone with an appointment. The hatch behind the incinerator is for people who still sweat. The choir door runs on an old Helion pad. I would not kiss it."

The penitent pass is a hundred. It scans often enough. Glass Chapel is three streets over. You leave the steam of the stall for its white light.

observations.text:
Antiseptic and cheap incense are losing a fight in here. A bowl of extracted optics waits under a sign that says RECYCLE in a font meant to be kind.

No one is shouting yet. You file that under temporary.

The chair room is up a short stair. Someone is humming a hymn with the rhythm taken out.

You came to keep your life yours. The chair upstairs offers to make that question simpler. You keep walking.

A nurse with a shaved head and an optic that refocuses like it resents the distance. Her hands are clean. Her shoes are not.

"You are not on the penitent list. Dawn puts Mara Voss in that chair so Helion can edit a crime out of her. The next sentence should be one you can survive."

observations.text:
"Mara Voss signed the coolant dump into Ward Nine. Three hundred people. One memo. No funeral that used their names. The shard is the only unedited hour.

Sell it to Quill and he sells it to Helion, and Helion buys the last copy of its own crime. Break it, and I leak what I remember. Memory is weaker than a shard. It is still a fire."

She waits. The optic is dark now, which means she is doing this as a person.

Mara Voss is under the halo, breathing on a four-count. The plinth is open for calibration. The shard is a tongue of glass, still warm from a life.

Lumen nods at the plinth. "Copy it. Then we both leave holding a fire. Do not get clever and die."

You have a minute before the door's patience ends.

observations.text:
The shard is warm against your palm, and it does not wait for you to be ready.

Mara's voice, unedited: "I signed the coolant dump. Ward Nine. Three hundred on the night shift. I want that sentence to stay in my mouth."

The halo would have taken it out of her by dawn. It is in your hand instead.

observations.text:
The hour is not finished with you.

Mara’s recorded voice, still unedited: "Helion told me the dump was a flush, not a kill. I signed because the night shift was already in the building and I thought the tower would move them. They did not move them."

She does not ask you to forgive it. She asks you to keep the reason attached to the crime.

Inspect each fragment. A claim needs a source, and a source can put a living person in danger.

observations.text:
The viewer holds three inspected fragments. Arrange their timestamps, replay Mara's recorded explanation, or carry a direct interpretation.

Her signature is visible. Her assurance is testimony, not proof the workers left. The receipt's issuer remains unverified; the exit log identifies a possible witness, not an account she has agreed to give.

What will you carry out?

The shard is already against your palm, warm as a coin left on an engine.

Sister Lumen stands at the halo controls with her hands open, so everyone can see she is not pressing them.

"Put it down." Kerr fills the door. The knee is the only apology on him. "That glass is Mara's hour. Helion pays me so the Ward Nine memo stays in her head, not in your pocket."

"You want me to decide this is somebody else's trouble. Tell me what it costs you."

observations.text:

"You can leave. Don't call it saving her."

observations.text:
You leave the original in the chair room. Kerr lets the space between you stay empty. You walk into the alley awake, without paying for another injury.

A copy remains in the buffer. It does not change where you left the original.

Quill will not pay for an original you did not deliver. The next week is still yours to enter.

The Week starts in the street. The week wants a buyer or a witness.

observations.text:
A week of rain has rewritten the paint. Quill's stall is dark. The bowls are stacked. He priced your absence and went home.

The tower you used to wear is still up there, pretending it does not know this street.

Ward Nine is still a direction people lower their voice to say.

Quill's tab is still in the steam, even when he will not look at you.

The route board is still there. The cards that know your name are the ones face up.

observations.text:
Between jobs the city offers cards, not streets. You stand under a cracked route board in Ward Four and the rain writes on it faster than the tower does.

Ward Four is Kerr. He collects. Glass Chapel is Lumen. She still has your name in a mouth that does not forget. The Spire is not asking. Yet.

The orderly from the basin is under the board, gold tooth, no coat. "Pass still scans," he says, and does not ask what you did with the hour.

Pick the door that knows you. The others can wait for a week you do not have.

observations.text:
Kerr is under the same awning, a week deeper into the rain. He wants the weight of the glass. He already knows you were in the room.

He offers the knee as the price of the conversation: what it cost him, what it should cost you.

"You can tell me what the hour was worth," he says, "or you can walk past and let the canal be the argument."

Kerr turns his wrist, looking for a clock he is not wearing tonight. The chapel has reached this awning ahead of you.

"You left the hour in the room. I stayed. Neither of us gets to call that a rescue."

observations.text:
Kerr is under the same awning Quill uses when he wants to look like a rumor. Quill is not here. That is the point.

The knee is a private weather system. He stands like the doorway owes him rent.

"Week's up," he says. "Helion paid me to know the weight of that glass. You are the part of the weight I can still invoice."

observations.text:
Last week the city called this Empty Hands. This week you stand where the noodle steam can hear you and you say Mara Voss's name next to Ward Nine until a stranger repeats it wrong, which is how a fact learns to walk.

Helion will answer. Quill will pretend he was never hungry. The wards will get it half right, and half right is more than a plinth ever offered.

The card for Ward Nine is still on the board. The people who lived there have not agreed to be a speech.

observations.text:
Sera stands you in front of the wall before she asks anything. ‘Jo.’ Sera uses your own name, then turns you toward the concrete. The rain has eaten the lower rows. One name needs no optic: Ivo Pell, night shift, level two.

You kept another name from the memo: Junie Calder, night shift, the locker beside Ivo.

"Ivo stays legible," Sera says. "The third row needs your eye, or help from the wards. You can try. You can also tell me why you came."

She waits with the pencil capped.

observations.text:
Coolant scars climb Ward Nine’s lower floors. The tower called the dump maintenance. The neighbors moved upstairs and wrote the names where they could still reach them.

Sera uncaps her pencil. She has kept the list through another week of rain.

The street version of the week got here before you did, wrong in the details and right about the tower.

"If you know any of them," she says, "say them. If you sold them, you can still say them. The wall does not check your receipt."

observations.text:
You leave the wall to the weather. You leave the proof where you left it last week.

Sera does not chase you. Ward Nine has practice at people who get to the stair and then remember they have somewhere dry to be. The names stay. The rain stays. You stay a person who could have spoken and did not, which is its own title.

Halfway down the stair you hear Sera set the pencil against the next line. She does not ask you to turn around. Her voice reaches you through the rain.

"Mind the broken step. It's the second one down."
visibleSummaries: Review every commitment and its limits
